message.text: `retire` builds and pushes a commit from the tip without judging the whole tree. It reads only the top level of `changesets/` (`StateTree.folders`) and the folders it removes (`judgeFolder`), and never calls `StateTree.read`/`refuse`. So a stray at the root, a file directly under `changesets/`, or a folder under a name no changeset can have does not refuse the call. `folders()` likewise answers from a tree it read only in part. The base location decision says such an entry "refuses every call on every changeset", and that "no call answers from a tree it has judged in part, and no push replaces a tree it has not judged whole". The base guideline says `StateTree` "judges every entry of the fetched tree before a call answers or builds a commit" and that a stray outside a folder "refuses every changeset".

evidence.snippet:
An unknown entry under `changesets/<A>/`, where `A` is a name the store accepts, refuses every call on `A`: `list`, `add`, `readCell`, `writeCell` and `dispose`. Calls on any other changeset go on. Examples: `changesets/A/notes.txt`; a symbolic link at `changesets/A/cell.json`; `changesets/A/finding/<hash>/<id>.json` whose bytes hash to another ID.

Any other unknown entry refuses every call on every changeset. Examples: an `index.json` at the root; `changesets/Bad Name!/x.json`, under a directory no changeset could be named; `changesets` itself as a file rather than a folder.

Each refusal is a `RecordError` with the code `unknownFile` that names the entry, and `melian doctor` names every unknown entry for a writer to remove.

### What the refusal still promises

Melian judges every entry of the tree it fetched before it answers a call or builds a commit, so a refused call returns no record, not even the known ones beside the stray, and pushes nothing. That is what "before a byte is read in part or pushed over" now means: no call answers from a tree it has judged in part, and no push replaces a tree it has not judged whole.

- `StateTree` judges every entry of the fetched tree before a call answers or builds a commit. An entry is known when it is a mode `100644` file at `changesets/<changeset>/cell.json` holding a cell Melian writes, or at the path a record's own bytes give. A stray in one changeset's folder refuses that changeset; a stray anywhere else refuses every changeset. A handle remembers what it judged by mode, type, object ID and path, so it reads each blob once, and an entry whose mode changes is judged again. A refusal or `melian doctor` names a path that is not UTF-8 in git's quoted form, as `git ls-tree` prints it, so two such names never read alike.

explanation.whatToDo: Choose one, then make code and decision agree. Either have `retire` (and `folders`) refuse with `unknownFile` when the tip holds a stray outside every changeset's folder, judging only the root and the top level of `changesets/` for that, which stays within the listing bound. Or add an explicit `Amends:` line to the location decision's "Two scopes" and "What the refusal still promises" sections, stating that a retirement is exempt and why, for the maintainer to rule on.
explanation.whyHere: This weakens a fail-closed rule, and the change does not declare it. The new decision's `Amends:` lines against the location decision cover only what a tip past a limit refuses and the resource table. Nothing amends the scope rule for unattributable strays, and the decision mentions only strays inside a folder. The tests at retire.test.ts:480 and :491 make the departure an asserted contract, so the scheduled job in PR C inherits a call that pushes onto a branch every other call refuses as `unknownFile`.

properties.failureScenario: A writer's older build or a hand push leaves `index.json` at the root of `melian/state`, or `changesets/Bad Name!/x.json`, or a blob at `changesets/pull-fedcba9876543210`. Under the base rule every call now fails with `unknownFile` naming that entry until a writer removes it: `add`, `list`, `readCell`, `writeCell` and `dispose` on every changeset. `store.retire(seen, merged)` on that tip still reads `folders()`, judges only the named folders, builds a commit with `withoutFolders`, and pushes it. `removesOnly` checks only that the commit removed whole changeset folders, not that the tree held no stray. The call returns `removed: [...]` with no word of the stray, so the scheduled job keeps pushing onto a branch the store's own rule says must stop all work. That is the reverse of the documented "refuses every call on every changeset" and "no push replaces a tree it has not judged whole". The tests "is not blocked by a stray at the root, and leaves it" (retire.test.ts:480) and "is not blocked by a file directly under `changesets/`" (:491) assert this behaviour.
